claims.claim: Reviewers note a lack of weapon and enemy variety.

citations.review_text: Absolutely incredible world design. The ornate and grandiose architecture gives the world a sense of scale I've never felt in a video game before. The combat is very satisfying as well. I would have liked to see some more enemy variety in the PvE modes and a campaign that doesn't treat the player like they are already a 40K expert who understands the stakes perfectly. Maybe I just need to bone up on the lore and it's my fault for being out of the loop, but I really had no idea what was going on story-wise while playing this.

I am a huge Warhammer 40k fan. I am only partially through the campaign at the moment and maybe there is more meat at the end of the game but overall I am just finding this game incredibly mid. I paid roughly $10

Some bullet-pointed thoughts:
- There's not enough weapon variety.
- There's not enough combat variety.
- The environment is okay but fails to impress in the way that I feel the setting deserves. For instance I think Armored Core 6 or Elden Ring has a much better invocation of scope and feel.
- I think the battles aren't big enough.
- The Tyranid swarms often feel too small.
- The story, acting, and pacing could be better.
- There's just a lot of little gripes I have.
I almost feel like Space Hulk: Deathwing is an overall better game if you want to capture the feel of facing Tyranid swarms.

I wish the game UI provided more information about the weapons aside from "mid range weapon, 3 round blast" and that the weapons had a bit more variation (and ammo, although finding ammo isn't hard). I also wish there was more diversity in what you do for each level (for the main story), such as using/riding a tank/controlling a vehicle (not sure if space marines even operate things like that..). However, as a new fan of the 40,000 universe, I think this is a good game to dip your toes into. And the graphics are amazing. solid 8/10, I had fun. For the Emperor!

The gameplay is boring and repetitive. The enemy variety is particularly disappointing, which is a shame in a Warhammer 40K game, where the setting offers so much potential for diverse opponents.

The highlight of the game is undoubtedly the final mission. It's clear that the developers put a lot of effort into it, and it really shows.

I thoroughly enjoyed the previous Space Marine game, but somehow this sequel fails to recapture the fun and excitement I experienced with its predecessor.

claims.claim: Combat relies heavily on parrying, dodging, and executing enemies to regenerate armor.

citations.review_text:
Sadly, as someone who isn't into Warhammer that much but was interested in Space Marines, this game doesn't appeal to me very much. Let me start off by saying that visually, this game was pretty good. The overall aesthetic was good, the art style was tight. I loved customizing my character. The progression was pretty grindy, but that's not a huge deal if the game hooks me. Even the dialogue, albeit somewhat enigmatic to me, was fine. 

What *was* a deal-breaker was the gameplay. The gameplay was awfully arcade-y, with it boiling down to spamming executions and countering into executions. The sound design for most weapons felt weak and unsatisfying. Levels were very linear and didn't offer a lot of replay-ability nor room for creativity. Most of the variety came from the different classes, which were interesting, but hard to get into when just starting out. On higher difficulties, enemies became extremely spongey and did a lot of damage to the point that you had to constantly do executions to regain armor so you didn't die. Getting stims was so infrequent that this became mandatory. Ammo reserves were terribly small, forcing you to constantly be looking for caches (no thanks to said sponges). Starting fresh was rough as lower difficulties were kind of a cakewalk while higher difficulties were unsatisfyingly hard for all the wrong reasons. It sucks since the grind is pretty long, and there are a ton of classes that seem neat, but require a lot of time to get up-to-snuff. It basically becomes 3rd person RPG, where your stats matter more than your skill. Enemies themselves were kind of forgettable. A lot of melee enemies that require you to either dodge or counter then execute. Ranged enemies, you just shoot them. About as much depth as Batman Arkham combat. 

I don't have anything to say about the PvP as I tend to stick to the PvE side of things. 

Now if you love Space Marines, then you'll probably *like* this game. If you don't but are interested in the franchise and…

Holy shit the combat is ass. Loved Space Marine 1 to bits, but that game was about combos and setting up executions, this one is all about parrying and dodging, with awful controls. Very unresponsive, very messy. Shame.

single_points.text: One reviewer says interacting requires holding down a button before the animation plays, with no option to turn it off.

citation.review_text:
Space Marine 0.8

Sure it looks a bit better graphically than the first game from 2011, but the gameplay has taken a massive step back.
It feels awful to shoot, it feels awful to melee, the story keeps slowing you down and halting your movement at points.

Hold button to interract, the biggest peeve of mine in modern gaming.
WHY NOT PLAY THE ANIMATION WHILE YOU ARE HOLDING DOWN THE BUTTON!?
instead you get:
1 "hold button to interract"-promt
2 *holding button to interract*
3 "plays animation after button has been held"

For every single button, at least picking up ammo boxes are instant.
And there is no option to turn that shit off.

And then we get to the shooting, and you just KNOW its a console game if there is aimclimb, because analog sticks can be held in a direction indefinitely to counteract the climb, meanwhile as a PC gamer you only have so much room to move the mouse. Also, no option to turn this off either.

After about 2 hours and a 100 GB download, i think ive had enough. this game is a piece of shit.

Enjoyment score is at 14%

Because the game is soooo daaamn large, ill keep it installed for a bit longer and maybe give it 1 more hour, but chances are im done with it.
I dont think the devs knew what they had with this IP.
If this game had been released 2-3 years after the first game i might have been a bit more impressed, but now in this day and age? its outdated, and severely so.
The guns feel like airsoft weapons and the melee weapons feel like pool noodles.
the game is air. a box of air.

If you want a [b]GOOD[/b] WH40k experience, play Darktide, its like night and day.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as short, leaving them wanting more missions and lore.

citations.review_text:
I LOVE THIS GAME the gameplay is insanely addicting and the story is painfully short but entirely complete. it runs well, looks amazing and perfectly introduces you into its little slice of the warhammer 40K universe. i cannot recommend this game enough

 FOR THE EMPEROR

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 was an incredible game and a huge leap in graphics, story and gameplay for the series. The campaign was unfortunately short and it was a shame because i was wanting more missions and lore and enemies to fight through, especially since i paid full price for the game too. The replay though does lie in the games multiplayer areas and unlocking skins and parts for your space marine customisation. It's essentially a barbie simulator but for warhammer space marines and using them in online matches too, against other players where you can have a car meet up for your space marine armours. 

I loved playing through the campaign and getting to see what happened to titus again. Hoping to hear more details and lore about what he went through and where he goes next. I will admit though bits of the campaign didn't feel as fresh or new in my eyes. Some parts felt very familiar and unoriginal, like it was ripped right from the first game and just improved upon story wise and graphically. For example in the first game, your space marine squad member leandros, gets suspicious of you and suspects heresy and turns you into the inqusition. The same situation happens in this game too, one of your squad mates suspects you of heresy and tried to kill you. 

I'm still not used to space marines 1 and 2 when it comes to the fighting mechanics and did get frustrated here and there when i got swarmed or died. It definitely takes some getting used to and can be quite rewarding once you've got it down and in a good rhythm. Overall it was a great game to go through and i did enjoy the story, what little of it there was and would easily recommend this game to anybody. Do beware of course that this game is mainly about customising your space marine and doing lots of multiplayer matches and modes too. If you enjoy either of…

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance issues including low frame rates and heavy stuttering during intense combat.

citations.review_text:
While I [b]did[/b] enjoy a lot of my time placing SM2, I can't recommend it to anyone who wants to spend some actual time on it. The game is fun, but it's just filled with small little issues that pile up and in the end you just feel like shit when thinking about them

The campaign is good. I have no idea how well it represents the actual Warhammer universe since this is basically my introduction to it, but I can say I like the characters, the lore and the world. How well the game showcases those things, I couldn't say. 

Onto the PvE is where shit gets weird. First of all, the game runs like shit. My setup isn't the most recent, but it can run most things pretty well, even recent releases without much issue. Space Marine just has something wrong with it. I mean that literally, I have tried putting the game on the lowest and the highest settings, and there is literally no difference in FPS.
Even heavy stuff like reflections, high shadows, no upscaling; game runs the same as when everything is set to low. And in heavier fights, it gets even worse. While playing siege (essentially the game's endless mode where waves get pretty insane as you go), my fps was hitting the low 20s, even going below that. I don't understand how the performance just doesn't change no matter what settings I mess around with.
Into the actual game, the missions are fun at first but can get repetitive. Right now, I'm pretty burned out of basically every mission, and while I do enjoy the gameplay I'm just done with the game's many bullshit points, such as:

- All of the weapons stats ARE WRONG. This is one of the most frustrating things to me, if you look at each stat on a weapon, gun or melee, everything is just wrong. You'd think the "firepower" stat would mean damage right? It does, except the number has jackshit to do with the actual damage! If a weapon has 1 firepower and you increase it to 2, that would mean it doubles, right? Fucking nope, it's probably more like 5-10%, that number is just…

Overall, the game is very good, but a few issues ended up completely ruining my experience...

First of all, it's the poor quality of the game servers. There have been many times when I was stuck in the lobby for more than 30 minutes doing matchmaking. During that time, I was forced to chat with other players, and they were suffering from the exact same issue as well. In the end, because the match never started, I would just quit the game entirely (and so would the other players).

Another issue is the game's performance, which has genuinely been a major problem, especially for me...
Based on my PC specs and what I've seen in the game's benchmarks, I should easily be getting between 50 and 65 FPS on high graphics settings. However, my FPS is ridiculously stuck below 30, and in some story mode missions, it even drops below 10...
I tried a bunch of different tweaks to fix this, but none of them made even the slightest difference in improving performance.

Given all these problems, unfortunately, I could never truly enjoy the game the way I should have. To be honest, out of every 5 times I launch the game, I can only play comfortably just 1 time, and that is just bad. ≡(▔﹏▔)≡

Played last October after the last update in a campaign mission. Game crashed so hard I had to safe reboot my PC and delete the corrupted game files. Have seen NO updates since then to address such an issue. I got this game to play as a righteous Space Marine, not have my computer infested with files so corrupted that it rivals the Chaos Gods.

The fact Saber hasn't done anything to fix these massive QOL issues and constantly breaks their own spaghetti code? Yeah, you should wait this one out until it's done being patched.

Also, to the damned warp with all these DLCs. 10 bucks per chapter pack which only adds some cosmetic pieces- some of which barely look different from others? Yeah, no, that's just predatory microtransaction slop and I hate it. I miss when Video Games just gave you all the cosmetic options by PLAYING THEM, not PAYING separately.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe severe multiplayer lag and matchmaking instability that disrupts gameplay.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Could've been great - Ended up being mediocre [/h1]

Game has VERY SERIOUS graphical performance issues on Steam Deck.

Also, the lag in multiplayer is so bad it's basically unplayable. I don't know if it's the servers or what, but it's some of the worst lag I've ever seen in a game before.

It's a shame really, because I wanted to like this game. But even if you overlook those two glaring issues, there's the dubious choice to link ARMOR REGENERATION, which is the way you "heal yourself" in combat, to in game [u] executions[/u] ala DOOM.

Why was that such a terrible decision? Because this isn't a singleplayer game. Meaning it's extremely easy for your "squadmates" to kill an enemy before you have a chance to use that enemy to regain your armor. Might not seem like a problem at first, but it makes playing with random players more trouble than it's worth, and mechanics like this really only belong in a singleplayer game like Doom. Just my opinion. Then again, they could've made it so the armor regen you get was a nice bonus, instead of making it a mandatory core mechanic of how you stay alive. [u] Oh, and Chaos enemies are extremely unfun to fight too. Even people who love this game will admit that. You can't have an entire faction that players actively avoid fighting. That's simply poor game design. [/u]

Sorry, but this game is only for the most casual gamer, who happens to be a  diehard Warhammer fan. Everyone else, steer clear of this game or you'll be sorely disappointed.

Virtually unplayable due to lags and failing servers for the last two months, which is unfortunate, as the game itself is good. Not sure if the problem lies on the side of developers, some bizarre security protocols on US part of the globe or our very own Roskompozor rampage, but the end result is essentially the same - you can't play. and by now I'm rather tired of doing the "shaman dance" around the disconnection issues.

This game is very fun when all the mechanics work as intended. unfortunately 70% of this games mechanics dont work when your even slightly laggy. even when you have a decent pc, 60% of the time your melee attacks, parrys and gun stricks dont count and dont stagger or stun the enemy like there ment to. normally this type of stuff is avoidable by having server regions and ways to make your own public game for others to join, which this games devs complitely ignore. which means you cant manually join games that are best fitted for you region and you just have to pray to the emperor that you get a server that doesnt remove your ability to survive.  i love this games but by god the lag just ruins everything and makes the game almost impossible

[this review was made right after i parried a lictor 3 times and all 3 gun stricks did nothing and i lost the match from a laser from a neurothrope hit me through a piller]

This game is broken more often than its working. Its very common for you to waste half an hour doing an activity only to have it bug out at the final loading screen resulting in nobody in your squad receiving any rewards. Each patch only seems to increase how frequently this occurs and worsen server stability. With all that said the game used to be great but the devs cant seem to figure out their spaghetti code nowadays.

Tactical role are most overworked and over equipped classes in the game with perks including double primary weapons, free equipment regeneration with better weapons than all classes combined and also the ability to carry a chain sword with double primary, grenades, health packs and perk bonuses for melee and ranged. 

The biggest problem is the unrealistic frame drops with game modes or even story scenes bricking my computer on low setting, I've got a 5060Ti / 64 GB ram the game feels like your typical console game engineered on the PC then ported from a console version.

Might not seem like a problem at first, but it makes playing with random players more trouble than it's worth, and mechanics like this really only belong in a singleplayer game like Doom. Just my opinion. Then again, they could've made it so the armor regen you get was a nice bonus, instead of making it a mandatory core mechanic of how you stay alive. [u] Oh, and Chaos enemies are extremely unfun to fight too. Even people who love this game will admit that. You can't have an entire faction that players actively avoid fighting. That's simply poor game design. [/u]

Sorry, but this game is only for the most casual gamer, who happens to be a  diehard Warhammer fan. Everyone else, steer clear of this game or you'll be sorely disappointed.

The Campaign
If you are looking for a good story with a good scale and interesting lore this game has got it and the difficulty of it was decent for the most part for an average player. I recommend the main campaign if you want to learn more about warhammer or are interesting in Titus (Same guy from secret level if you are searching for information after seeing it).

PvE
The PvE content has two primary modes that being Operations and Siege there is technically a third but I'll explain that later.
Operations are campaign style modes that take place alongside the main story timeline wise until a certain point. If you are wanting to play with your own special armor and cosmetics this is where you go and as you level up your class you unlock more cosmetics for that character AND THAT ONE ONLY the others you will have to grind on them as well even for the same cosmetic you earned on another class. This is clearly just a means to make retention without giving you anything new. Much of the cosmetic content is also locked behind DLC and essentially microtransactions which considering the game said it wouldn't have those is disappointing to see. The operations themselves are for the most part well balanced if not suffering now and then from the new enemies added when chaos spawn were first added they were 3 separate attack patterns with very little differntiation on the enemy and they could move inside each other (I have not tried operations since they added the chaos spawn and I fought them the first time I'll update this after I do again). The bosses or the latest one called The Vortex Beast is beatable but extremely difficult for a lower leveled player simply because of attack spam if you are a more melee oriented class it is painful. my love for warhammer and my crippling addiction to this game tells me i should be nicer, but i cant, lol. 
DLCs lock cosmetics in intervals and make you spend more and more money overtime just to look cool, instead of being bundled together, expanded, or discounted with the games age. something the first game did great was the bundling of DLCs. this game dramatically fails to give your wallet a break.
and despite all of the funding spent on the DLCs, the game on its own is rarely improved, in a constant loop of new operation, new heroic, and a spinoff of existing game modes + new DLC. storylines past the campaign are forgettable at best, fighting enemies is exhausting instead of interesting, etc. genuinely, most of what keeps me playing now is PVP and stratagems, because atleast with every match you're getting something new. crucible is horrible.

things i personally find odd and maybe worth changing;
- bulwark in pvp. holy shit... you'd think that they'd nerf the shield from the operations status (it can take sniper shots and zoan hits... etc) but they really didn't. the shield has no ability to get disabled and makes bulwarks hilariously difficult to hit if they're spamming it. maybe at least a "stamina" bar for keeping it up, yo...
- how damage is handled. enemies should not be getting spongier and weapons should not be so little damage. the little horde enemies shouldn't be taking 3 hits on absolute, regardless of if it is absolute. the damage they deal to you should be scaling with difficulty, and mostly alone. not their raw constant hp. also enemy enraging is ridiculous at times! at least make it wear off sooner or don't make them constantly run away, don't spam blocks and  don't spam unparriables.
- ability timers. classes should be defined by their ability, not just their specific war gear restrictions... assault dash builds do great, but i used to personally prefer ground pounds, and the damage output just didn't justify the cooldown on my ability. the aus…

Most expensive dress up game ever that goes for the DLCs and your time, you can make some really cool looking marines with all the little pieces and then have them fight. The larping is pretty fun and the players I met were good spirited about the game, the story mode was pretty good too. 

Game looks Gorgeous but can crash if your PC isn't to spec.

Sace Marines 2 is definitely made for people who like difficulty and the skill expression that comes after that, if you don't have an interest in going to forums and tutorials to learn how the game's systems work to complete higher difficulties you may as well not even bother on this game as 65% of it is doing everything again but harder. 

I had my fun but you get how it all loops ad infinitum after about 100 hours. Maybe in a few years there will be more content to enjoy.

Only negative because there isn't a middle option. Get this in a bundle during an anniversary so it's nice and cheap. You are going to be buying $300 worth of skins in a full price game after all.
